A Reward of $5000.00 (subject of Reward Notice
No.1899) has been offered for information leading to the
arrest of the person(s) responsible for the bombing of
the Grantown Ballroom, 33 Ningpo Road of the 7.3.1942.
The above ballroom re-opened to business on
the 4.4.1942. Special precautions are being taken to
prevent a repetition of the terrorist activities and
Chinese detectives are being placed inside the hall
from 11.a.m. until closing time daily. Similar duties
are being arranged for Uniform Branch in the foyers and
approaches to the ballroom.
Efforts have been made by the detective staff
to obtain information likely to bring about arrests in the
case but no success has yet been experienced. It is
understood that the Japanese Gendarmerie have at present
nothing to hand regarding the affair.

14th. April 42.

Brief details of bombing of
Grantown Ballroom, 7.3.1942.

At 8.45.p.m. on 7.3.1942 a report was received
at this station to the effect that a bomb had been
thrown in the Grantown Ballroom, 33 Ningpo Road.
A Police party immediately responded and
were augmented by Japanese Gendarmes and Naval Landing
Party details.
It was found that an explosion had taken place
in the west side of the ballroom and that 2 Japanese
and 15 Chinese had been injured. Of this number one
Chinese (a member of the serving staff) succumbed to
his injuries.
450 persons, Japanese Foreign and Chinese,
were brought to station and were interrogated by
Police and Military but no useful information could
be obtained and these persons were released.
The damage to the ballroom was extensive but
careful search failed to discover the form of explosive
used. None of the injured persons had shrapnel wounds
which suggests that the bomb was made of some powerful
blasting composition and contained in possibly a glass
or similar container.

1942年3月7日格兰登舞厅爆炸案简要详情。

1942年3月7日晚8时45分，本捕房接到报告，称宁波路33号格兰登舞厅内有人投掷炸弹。
警方小队立即出警，并得到日本宪兵和海军陆战队分队的增援。
经查，舞厅西侧发生爆炸，造成2名日本人和15名中国人受伤。其中一名中国人（服务人员）因伤重不治身亡。
450名日本人、外侨和中国人被带至捕房，接受警方和军方讯问，但未获得有用信息，这些人随后被释放。
舞厅受损严重，但经仔细搜查，未能发现所用炸药的形态。伤者均无弹片伤，这表明炸弹由某种强力爆破混合物制成，可能装于玻璃或类似容器中。

Tsaung Chiao

Ningpo
Central Stn.           17/3/42

Tsaung Chiao, age 24, a native of Ningpo, M/proprietor of the
Hoo Sing Sugar Hong at No.3 Tang Nan Li, Taku Road, residing at
No.62 Ma Loh Li, Avenue Edward VII.
    At about 8p.m. on March 7th, I went to the Grantown Ball-
room. After one dance, I sat on a sofa at the middle of the
west side. About 15 minutes later, I heard the sound of
explosion. I was injured and became senseless, lying on the
ground. I was later conveyed to the Lester Chinese Hospital
where I found that I had sustained injuries on my hands, feet,
face and right ear. I was detained in the hospital until
today. But I have not fully recovered yet.
    The above is my true statement.

                        Signed Tsaung Chiao.

庄乔，24岁，宁波人，大沽路塘南里3号胡兴盛糖行经理，住爱多亚路马乐里62号。
    3月7日晚8时许，我前往格兰登舞厅。跳了一支舞后，我坐在西侧中间的沙发上。约15分钟后，我听到爆炸声。我受伤并失去知觉，倒在地上。后来我被送往雷士德华人医院，发现我的手、脚、脸和右耳受伤。我在医院被扣留至今。但我尚未完全康复。

Tsaung Tsung
Soochow
Central 16-3-42.

Tsaung Tsung, age 29, a native of Soochow, residing at
Lane 434/9, Avenue Road.
I am a secretary employed by the Reserve Board of the
Shanghai Native Bank Guild situated at Lane 437, No.6 Szechuen
Road(The Reserve Board was established on the approval of the
Asia Development Bureau).
At 8p.m. on 7-3-42, I went to the Asia Development Restaur-
ant to take my dinner where I learned that my friend named
Ling Hong Nee who is a clerk employed the Land Tax Bureau of
the Shanghai City Government, had requested me to see him at the
Grantown Ballroom on Ningpo Road near Kiangse Road.
After taking my dinner at about 8.20p.m. I left the Asia
Development Restuarant, 813 North Szechuene Road and proceeded
to the above ballroom. I entered the ballroom via the right
door and therein I found Ling Hong Nee. We sat by a table at
the middle of the right side(west) of the dance floor. It was
at about 8.40p.m. when a bomb exploded at my right side, about
3 or 4 yards away resulting in my head and feet being injured.
I was later conveyed by ambulance to the Lester Chinese
Hospital together with 4 others, one of whom died as a result
of severe injuries while another one had already been discharged
from the hospital. I and Tsen Zai Ming were discharged from
hospital today. At present there is only one injured man
detained in hospital. I have recovered after 9 days treatment
in the hospital.
This is my true statement.
Signed Tsaung Tsung.

庄宗
苏州
中央捕房 1942年3月16日。

庄宗，29岁，苏州人，住爱文义路434弄9号。
我是上海钱业公会储备委员会（位于四川中路6号437弄，该储备委员会是经亚洲开发局批准成立的）雇佣的秘书。
1942年3月7日晚8时，我去亚洲开发餐厅吃晚饭，得知我的朋友林洪尼（音译）（上海市政府地政局职员）请我在靠近江西路的宁波路格兰登舞厅见他。
晚上8点20分左右吃完晚饭后，我离开北四川路813号的亚洲开发餐厅，前往上述舞厅。我从右侧门进入舞厅，在那里见到了林洪尼。我们坐在舞池右侧（西）中间的一张桌子旁。大约晚上8点40分，一枚炸弹在我右侧约3或4码处爆炸，导致我的头部和脚部受伤。
后来我和其他4人一起被救护车送往雷士德华人医院，其中一人因重伤死亡，另一人已出院。我和曾才明（音译，对应前文周才明或另一人，原文Tsen Zai Ming）今天出院。目前只有一名伤者仍留在医院。经过9天的住院治疗，我已康复。
这是我的真实陈述。
庄宗 签。

Tseu Zai Ming

Din-hai
Central          16-3-42.

    Tseu Zai Ming, age 23, native of Din-hai, Chekiang, resid-
ing at 426 Peking Road. I have been employed as a clerk at the
Toyo Cotton Coy., 185 Szechuen Road.
    At 2.30p.m. 7-3-42, I left Bing Woo Coy and proceeded home.
Later, my friends namely Zah Kya Tsong, Zee Yah Lee, Loh Yah Nyi
and Zung Yang Lai telephoned to me and arranged to meet them at
the Grantown after supper. At about 7.15p.m. I attended the
cabaret where I danced four times with a dancing girl name
unknown, who was requested by my friend to sit at the table.
Meanwhile an explosion occurred, and I laid down on the floor.
As there was fire in my front I immediately rushed underneath
a confectionary stall. I was subsequently removed to the
Lester Chinese Hospital where I was detained for treatment for
9 days. On the 16-3-42 I was discharged from the said hospital
and I was instructed to attend the doctor daily as an O.P.D.
patient.
RW  The above is my true statement.

周才明

定海
中央捕房          1942年3月16日。

    周才明，23岁，浙江定海人，住北京路426号。我一直在四川北路185号的东洋棉花公司担任职员。
    1942年3月7日下午2时30分，我离开炳吴公司（音译）回家。后来，我的朋友查家松（音译）、李雅礼（音译）、罗雅尼（音译）和钟杨来（音译）给我打电话，约定晚饭后在格兰登舞厅见面。晚上7点15分左右，我来到歌舞厅，与一名姓名不详的舞女跳了四次舞，她是应我朋友之邀坐在桌边的。此时发生爆炸，我倒在地上。由于面前起火，我立即躲到一个糖果摊下面。随后我被送往雷士德华人医院，在那里接受治疗并被扣留9天。1942年3月16日，我从该医院出院，并被告知每天作为门诊病人去看医生。
RW 以上是我的真实陈述。

10.3.1942. Station Office.

On the afternoon of the 10.3.1942 instructions were received from the Japanese Gendarmerie to the effect that the suspects detained at station be released but that those residing in the new blockaded area be returned to their respective homes within the blockade. 108 persons (37 males and 71 females) were at that time in police custody and of these 107 resided outside the blockade and were, after strong caution and warning, released at 5.15.p.m. 10.3.1942. The remaining male Chinese residing at 24 Ningpo Road was later escorted to and placed within the barricades.

A detailed list is being prepared showing full particulars of all arrested persons and their disposal and this will be submitted in due course.

In Diary No.C it was incorrectly reported that four suspects had been released by D.I.Mcaskill upon the guarantee of one Tsang Lee Fong. It has since been ascertained that the release was authorised by Major Saito, Japanese Military Special Section, 6 Great Western Road.

Further report will be submitted.

The scene of the bombing at 33 Ningpo Road has been photographed by D.S.Knowles, F.P.Bureau and these photographs have already been submitted.

On the morning of the 8.3.1942 an examination was made of the scene but no bomb fragments could be found. D.I.Ewins assisted in this search. As far as can be ascertained none of the injured persons had any bomb fragments in their wounds and, as none have been found at scene of crime, it is thought possible that the explosives were contained in some easily destroyed or combustible container or in glass.

On the morning of the 9.3.1942 the Japanese Gendarmerie submitted to station a chair cover containing glass particles and a small quantity of black powderlike substance. This was part of the substance obtained from the floor of the cabaret during examination and request was made for same to be analysed. Immediate report was made to D.O."A" Division and with his written authority the substance was handed over to the Chief Analyst at 3.00.p.m. 9.3.1942.

宁波路33号爆炸现场已由法医局诺尔斯侦探警长（D.S. Knowles）拍照，这些照片已提交。

1942年3月8日上午对现场进行了检查，但未发现炸弹碎片。尤因斯副督察（D.I. Ewins）协助了此次搜查。据查，伤者伤口中均无炸弹碎片，且犯罪现场也未发现碎片，因此认为爆炸物可能装在某种易毁或易燃容器中，或装在玻璃容器中。

1942年3月9日上午，日本宪兵队向巡捕房提交了一个含有玻璃颗粒和少量黑色粉末状物质的椅套。这是检查期间从歌舞厅地板上获取的部分物质，并要求对其进行分析。随即向“A”分区警官作了报告，并在其书面授权下，该物质于1942年3月9日下午3时移交给了首席化验师。

On Saturday the 7th.March I was on 2nd day duty
and between 7.p.m. and 11.p.m. was posted to the Grantown
Ballroom, 33 Ningpo Road. I, together with C.P.C.2389 was
posted to the foyer outside the ballroom on the 1st.floor.
During the time I was on duty I did not see anyone
enter the cabaret with any parcels, of any description, most
of the people leaving their coats etc. in the cloakroom which
adjoins the foyer.
At 8.40.p.m. I heard a loud explosion in the ballroom
and, together with C.P.C.2389, drew my pistol with the intent-
ion of stopping anyone leaving the dance floor but there was
such a rush that I was unable to prevent the guests and girls
from entering the foyer. C.P.C.2389 ran downstairs to use
the telephone whilst I guarded next to the cigarette counter
there being an exit by which persons could proceed to the
upper floors. Such was the crowd that I was unable to see
clearly what was going on but I saw two injured people carried
out of the ballroom and placed near me on the cigarette
counter.
Shortly afterwards the station police party arrived
and took over enquiries. During the time I was on duty I saw
many persons arrive and leave the premises but I cannot
recall any particular party nor did I see anything or person
which made me suspicious.

Central Stn.          9.3.1942

I was on second day duty on Saturday the 7.3.1942
and between 7.00.p.m. and 11.p.m. was posted to the Grantown
Ballroom, 33 Ningpo Road. I was posted in the foyer on the
1st.floor whilst C.P.C.57 was with me and C.P.C.3137 at the
main entrance on Ningpo Road.

At 8.40.p.m. an explosion occurred. At that time I
was standing in the foyer near the west side entrance to the
ballroom. I immediately drew my pistol and at that moment
many people both patrons and dance girls rushed out of the
dance floor crowded into the foyer, screaming and shouting.
Although there are two telephones in the foyer it was impos-
sible to use these and I ran downstairs to C.P.C.3137 with the
intention of using an outside telephone. C.P.C.3137 told me
that he had already reported to station and I therefore remained
with him guarding the main exit. At that time I saw Japanese
marines guarding the roadway outside the ballroom.

I did not see anyone enter the ballroom with a
parcel but when I arrived on duty the cabaret had already
been open since noon. I did not enter the actual ballroom
my duty being to remain in the foyer.

I cannot recall having seen any Chinese or Koreans
leave the hall immediately prior to the explosion but, during
the time I was on duty, many people arrived and left. I can
throw no light on the bombing or the possible identity of the
responsible parties.

Ry

C.P.C. 2389.

page_data.en:
At 8.45.p.m. on 7.3.1942 C.I.C. 3137
telephoned to station to the effect that a bomb
had been thrown at the Wei Kong (偉宮 )(Grantown)
Ballroom, 33 Ningpo Road. Station alarm bells
were rung and a party of police under C.D.I.Boddy
immediately responded.

On arrival at the scene of the bombing
it was found that the premises were already under
guard of the Japanese Naval Landing Party and it
was later ascertained that at precisely the time
the explosion occurred a Naval landing patrol was
passing the ballroom and, upon hearing the report
immediately took precautions.

It was found that an explosion causing
extensive damage and several injuries had occurred
on the west side of the ballroom just off the dance
floor. Several persons were found to be suffering
from injuries, three obviously very serious. A
fire had followed the explosion and, although this
had been extinguished by members of the ballroom
staff and orchestra, the S.F.Brigade and Emergency
Ambulances were called.

All persons found in the ballroom were
held and after all had been removed from the prem-
ises were, by arrangement between C.D.I.Boddy,
C.D.I. Himmiya and Lieut. Tanita (acting in charge
of the J.N.L.P. detachment, brought to station.

Upon the nature of the affair becoming
known the Reserve Unit was called and all bridges

1942年3月7日晚上8点45分，华探 C.I.C. 3137

炸弹。巡捕房警报铃响起，由副督察 Boddy
率领的一队警察立即出动。

到达爆炸现场后，发现该场所已由日本海
军陆战队看守，后经查实，在爆炸发生的准
确时刻，一支海军登陆巡逻队正经过舞厅，
听到响声后立即采取了预防措施。

经查，舞厅西侧紧邻舞池处发生爆炸，造
成严重破坏和多人受伤。发现数人受伤，其
中三人伤势显然非常严重。爆炸后发生了火
灾，虽然舞厅工作人员和乐队成员已将其扑
灭，但仍呼叫了上海救火会 (S.F.Brigade)
和紧急救护车。

As a result of lengthy enquiries the following
brief details of the affair are known:-

The cabaret which is Chinese owned and is
managed by Wong Ziang Fah opened for business at noon
on 7.3.1942. C.D.C.39 and C.D.C.10 were detailed for
observation duty and at the time of the outrage C.D.C.
10 and C.P.Cs 57, 2389 and 3137 were on duty, the C.D.C.
in the ballroom and the C.P.Cs outside.

there was a brilliant flash and loud report from the
west side of the room, midway between the band and exits.
The explosion caused considerable damage and, owing to
heavy smoke and dust, the assembly was enveloped in a
mist. Interrogation tends to show that the seat of the

经过长时间调查，已知该事件的简要细节如
下：

该歌舞厅由华人拥有，由王祥发管理，于
1942年3月7日中午开始营业。华探 C.D.C.39
和 C.D.C.10 被指派执行观察任务，案发时
华探 C.D.C.10 以及警员 C.P.Cs 57、2389
和 3137 正在执勤，华探在舞厅内，警员在
外面。

1942年3月7日晚，舞厅出人意料地宾客盈
门，应特别要求，乐队刚开始演奏，大约演
奏了2或3分钟，此时约有30到40对伴侣进
入舞池，突然房间西侧、乐队与出口之间的
中部位置出现一道强光和巨大的响声。爆炸
造成了相当大的破坏，由于浓烟和灰尘，整
个集会场所笼罩在一片迷雾中。讯问情况表
明，爆

and a table and that smoke was first seen near the
floor, rising upwards. Although it is possible that
the bomb was thrown it appears more likely that same
was hidden under or near the settee. The damage done
suggests that the bomb was of considerable size and/or
power.

Persons sitting and dancing near the seat of
the explosion were thrown to the floor and such was the
blast that instruments were knocked from the hands of
the musicians. Although some parties stated that the
report accompanying the explosion was very loud others
stated that it appeared somewhat muffled. In this conn-
ection it must be noted that the ceiling of this room
is unusually low and this, together with the fact that
the hall was crowded and the band was playing, would
tend to lessen the noise whilst increasing the effect.
Immediately after the explosion panic ensued. Patrons,
taxi dancers and male staff immediately attempted to
leave the hall by the two normal exits on the north end
and by emergency exits at the south end. In the south-
east corner of the room there was a window, boarded up
with ply wood. This was smashed and some persons left
by this means. It is known that three teenagers and one

炸中心位于长沙发附近，或沙发与桌子之
间，且烟雾首先出现在靠近地板处，向上升
腾。虽然有可能是投掷炸弹，但更有可能的
是炸弹被藏在沙发下面或附近。造成的破坏
表明炸弹体积较大和/或威力巨大。

坐在爆炸中心附近跳舞的人被震倒在地，爆
炸冲击波之大，甚至将乐器从乐手手中震落。
虽然有些人声称伴随爆炸的响声非常大，但
其他人则表示声音似乎有些沉闷。在此必须
指出，该房间的天花板异常低矮，加上大厅
拥挤且乐队正在演奏，这些因素往往会减弱
噪音，同时增加爆炸效果。爆炸发生后立即
陷入恐慌。顾客、出租车舞女和男性工作人
员立即试图通过北端的两个正常出口和南端
的紧急出口离开大厅。房间东南角有一扇窗
户，用胶合板封住。窗户被砸碎，一些人由
此离开。已知有三名青少年和一名

have since been detained by police.
C.D.C.10, on duty in the ballroom stated that
he saw no one enter with any parcel but at 8.40.p.m.
was sitting at the north-east corner of the floor near
the door. The dance floor was well covered when the
explosion occurred and everyone appeared to rush for
the exits. He attempted to make report to station
but as the telephone has an extension which was then
in use he was unable to make direct contact and was
about to leave the building when the J.M.P. patrol
and he was held inside.
By arrangements between police, Lieut.Tomita
and Special Sargt-Major Sudo of the Gendarmerie all
the patrons and staff of the ballroom and all persons
found in the surrounding buildings were brought to
station for further interrogation. These totalled
40 Japanese (male & Female), 8 foreigners (orchestra)
72 Dance girls, 161 male Chinese, 79 Chinese females
and 58 children, 39 male Chinese (staff of ballroom)

undertaken by all staff assisted by Japanese detectives
from Special Branch but, so far, no light has been
thrown on the affair.

在舞厅内执勤的华探 C.D.C.10 称，他没有
看到任何人携带包裹进入，但在晚上8点40

发生时舞池挤满了人，大家似乎都冲向出口。
他试图向巡捕房报告，但由于电话分机当时
正在使用中，他无法直接联系，正当他准备
离开大楼时，日本军事警察 (J.M.P.) 巡逻
队赶到，他被拦在室内。

安排，舞厅的所有顾客和工作人员以及在周

所有工作人员在日本特高科侦探的协助下对
这些人进行了讯问，但截至目前，尚未查明
事件真相。

page_data.en:
Upon completion of station interrogation all
Japanese subjects, the male staff of the ballroom and
the orchestra were handed over to the Japanese Gendarmerie
together with one female and three male Chinese connected
with the Gendarmerie and City Government. The remainder
of the detained persons are held at station pending
further instructions as to their disposal.

As a result of above enquiries it is learned
that No.8 teaboy, Toong Zung Ziang, now deceased, was
in attendance at the tables nearest the seat of the
explosion. No.11 boy Foo Tsai Kung ( 傅再根 ) and No.
10 boy Bah Vong Ziang ( 白凤祥 ) who were also serving
in that section stated that there were two male Chinese
sitting at a table but that when the music started they
proceeded onto the dance floor. These two boys were
carefully escorted around all the suspects both Japanese
and Chinese but were unable to identify the persons
referred to by them. It is possible that these two
did leave the ballroom but it is also possible that
the two patrons were Japanese and are the two now de-
tained seriously injured in Pootung Hospital.

and Lah Yeh Kyi ( 陸学義 ) claim to have been sitting
